title: refactor: simplify text provider adapters
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces lenient Azure endpoint extraction with one validated parser and removes duplicated deployment arguments from 17 model configs.
- Replaces Cohere's hand-written SSE buffering with the existing `eventsource-parser` stream and consolidates boundary control-token stripping.
- Preserves Azure resource/deployment/API-version routing, provider overrides, split-token handling, choice metadata, malformed JSON pass-through, and request rejection behavior.
- Consolidates #12948 into this draft: 3 files changed, 106 insertions, 145 deletions (39 net lines removed).

Checks:
- Focused Azure resolver, parameter, and Cohere sanitizer suites — 34 passed, including all 9 Cohere cases
- All 69 `portkeyConfig` factories resolved
- Strict Azure parser assertions for malformed hosts, deployment paths, and missing API versions
- Gen `npm run typecheck`
- Biome on all 3 changed files
- `git diff --check`

Supersedes #12948.

gist.headline: Adapters shed their husks
gist.blurb: The text-provider plumbing got a careful pruning: one Azure parser, one Cohere event stream, and 39 fewer lines to keep watered. Polli labels the cables while the providers continue behaving exactly as intended.
gist.summary: Refactored gen's Azure and Cohere text-provider adapters by replacing lenient Azure endpoint extraction with a validated parser, removing 17 duplicated deployment arguments, and using eventsource-parser for Cohere SSE sanitization.
gist.impact: Azure resource/deployment/API-version routing and Cohere split-token, choice-metadata, malformed-JSON, and rejection handling remain intact with less duplicated adapter logic to maintain.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-shed server room where Polli tidies two provider pipes: an Azure-blue-but-pastel route map feeding a clearly labeled parser box, and a Cohere event stream flowing through a small sieve that catches control-token leaves. Polli wears a tiny mechanic tool belt while code-plants grow around the organized cables, representing a simpler internal path without changing the output.
